work.abstract_text: We give an alternative proof of both clauses of Ivan N. Ianakiev's August 20, 2019 conjecture in OEIS A094373 (revision 86, comment at export line 13) from the Zimin-word theorem of Fici, Gagie, Kärkkäinen and Kempa (2014, Section 5, Lemma 12 and its proof) and the factorial-plateau identity of Kullmann and Zhao (2015, Lemma 3.11): the shortest nontrivial palindrome starting at position i>=2 in the run-length sequence of A007843 has length 2^(nu_2(i-1)+1)+1. Equal endpoint valuations give the lower bound, and reflection about a multiple of a larger power of two attains it. Consequently, the complete first-occurrence list is 1,2,3,5,9,..., and P(A(m-1))=A(m) for every m>=2. We also characterize every palindromic factor, transfer the same minima to divisor-power quotients, and deduce Ianakiev's four related assertions on A296306, crediting the earlier answers of Hasler and Bala.

work.title: An alternative proof of Ianakiev's shortest-palindrome conjecture via Fici and collaborators' Zimin-word theorem
